name: Gateway of India
short_description: Iconic 26-metre basalt arch monument built in 1924, overlooking Mumbai Harbour. One of India's most photographed landmarks.

name: Elephanta Caves
short_description: UNESCO World Heritage rock-cut cave temples dedicated to Lord Shiva, located on Elephanta Island in Mumbai Harbour.

name: Marine Drive
short_description: A 3.6 km long boulevard along the coast of South Mumbai, known as the Queen's Necklace due to its night-time appearance.

name: Siddhivinayak Temple
short_description: One of the most visited Ganesh temples in India, located in Prabhadevi. Receives millions of devotees annually.

name: Juhu Beach
short_description: A 6 km long beach in the western suburbs of Mumbai, famous for street food, sunset views and celebrity sightings.

name: Haji Ali Dargah
short_description: A mosque and dargah located on a tidal islet off the coast of Worli in the Arabian Sea, built in 1431.

name: Sanjay Gandhi National Park
short_description: A 104 sq km national park within Mumbai city limits, home to leopards, deer and the ancient Kanheri Caves.

name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Vastu Sangrahalaya
short_description: Maharashtra's premier museum with over 50,000 exhibits including ancient Indian art, natural history and archaeology.

name: Aga Khan Palace
short_description: Italian-style palace built in 1892, served as prison for Mahatma Gandhi and Kasturba Gandhi during 1942-44. Houses a Gandhi memorial museum.

name: Dagdusheth Halwai Ganpati Temple
short_description: One of Pune's most famous Ganesh temples, founded in 1893 by sweet-maker Dagdusheth Halwai. Decorated with gold and jewels worth crores.

name: Osho International Meditation Resort
short_description: World-famous spiritual retreat and meditation center covering 40 acres in Koregaon Park, attracting visitors from over 100 countries.

name: Mulshi Lake
short_description: A scenic reservoir in the Sahyadri hills, surrounded by lush forests and waterfalls, popular for camping and picnics.

name: Ajanta Caves
short_description: UNESCO World Heritage rock-cut Buddhist cave monuments from 2nd century BCE to 480 CE. Contains 30 caves with ancient paintings and sculptures.

name: Ellora Caves
short_description: UNESCO World Heritage site with 34 rock-cut temples representing Buddhist, Hindu and Jain faiths, built between 6th-11th centuries.

name: Bibi Ka Maqbara
short_description: Known as the Taj of the Deccan, this 17th century Mughal tomb was built by Aurangzeb in memory of his wife Dilras Banu Begum.

name: Grishneshwar Temple
short_description: One of the twelve Jyotirlingas (sacred Shiva shrines) in India, located near Ellora. Built in red Yeola stone in the 18th century.

name: Lonar Crater Lake
short_description: A 52,000-year-old hyper-velocity meteorite impact crater lake. One of only four known alkaline meteorite lakes in the world.

name: Trimbakeshwar Temple
short_description: One of the twelve Jyotirlingas, located near the source of Godavari River. Site of Kumbh Mela every 12 years.

name: Sula Vineyards
short_description: India's largest and most visited winery, producing award-winning wines. Offers wine tours, tastings and resort accommodation.

name: Pandav Leni Caves
short_description: 24 ancient Buddhist rock-cut caves dating back to 1st century BCE, featuring inscriptions and carvings in the hillside near Nashik.

name: Kalaram Temple
short_description: 400-year-old black stone Lord Rama temple in Panchavati, Nashik. Historically significant as the site where Dr. Ambedkar led a Satyagraha in 1930.

name: Ganpatipule
short_description: A famous self-emerged Swayambhu Ganesh temple on the Konkan coast with a pristine white sand beach. Considered spiritually powerful.

name: Tarkarli Beach
short_description: Maharashtra's best known beach for its crystal-clear waters and coral reefs. Famous for scuba diving, snorkeling and water sports.

name: Alibaug Beach
short_description: Popular beach destination near Mumbai, accessible by ferry. Known for Kolaba Fort, black sand beaches and fresh seafood.

name: Lonavala
short_description: Popular hill station between Mumbai and Pune at 625m altitude. Famous for monsoon waterfalls, chikki, and scenic Sahyadri valleys.

name: Mahabaleshwar
short_description: Maharashtra's most popular hill station at 1372m, known for strawberries, viewpoints and the origin of 5 rivers. Closed to tourists during monsoon.

name: Matheran
short_description: Asia's only automobile-free hill station at 800m altitude. Accessible only by toy train, horses or on foot. Known for red laterite paths and panoramic views.

name: Panchgani
short_description: A hill station at 1334m famous for its Table Land (second largest mountain plateau in Asia), strawberry farms and boarding schools.

name: Bhimashankar
short_description: One of the twelve Jyotirlingas, located within the Bhimashankar Wildlife Sanctuary â€” home to the Giant Indian Squirrel. Popular trekking destination.

name: Lavasa
short_description: India's first planned hill city, built along the Warasgaon Lake with Italian-inspired architecture. Popular for lakeside promenades and adventure sports.

name: Shirdi Sai Baba Temple
short_description: One of India's most visited pilgrimage sites with over 25,000 visitors daily. Dedicated to Sai Baba who lived here from 1858 to 1918.

name: Shani Shingnapur
short_description: Famous Shani temple village where houses have no doors or locks â€” a tradition upheld for centuries due to belief in Shani's protection.

name: Pandharpur
short_description: Maharashtra's spiritual capital on the banks of Bhima River. The Vitthal-Rukmini Temple attracts millions during Wari pilgrimage.

name: Kolhapur Mahalaxmi Temple
short_description: One of the 18 Shakti Peethas (seats of the goddess Shakti), dedicated to Goddess Mahalaxmi. The original temple was built in 7th century CE.

name: Tuljapur Bhavani Temple
short_description: Tuljabhavani is the Kuladevi (family deity) of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj and the Bhosale clan. One of the Shaktipeethas in Maharashtra.

name: Ashtavinayak â€” Moreshwar Temple Morgaon
short_description: First and most important of the eight Ashtavinayak shrines. The presiding deity Moreshwar (Mayureshwar) is depicted sitting on a peacock.

name: Tadoba Andhari Tiger Reserve
short_description: Maharashtra's oldest and largest national park, with one of India's highest tiger densities. Also home to leopards, sloth bears and wild dogs.

name: Melghat Tiger Reserve
short_description: One of India's first Project Tiger reserves, set in the Satpuda mountain range. Home to tigers, leopards, gaur and over 300 bird species.

name: Radhanagari Wildlife Sanctuary
short_description: Maharashtra's first wildlife sanctuary, home to the Indian gaur (bison), leopards, deer and over 230 bird species in the Western Ghats.

name: Nagpur Zero Mile Stone
short_description: The geographical centre of India, marked by a British-era stone monument. A symbolic landmark representing the heart of the nation.

name: Deekshabhoomi
short_description: Sacred site where Dr. B.R. Ambedkar and 600,000 followers converted to Buddhism on October 14, 1956. Houses a massive stupa built in 2001.

name: Pench National Park
short_description: Inspiration for Rudyard Kipling's The Jungle Book. Pench Tiger Reserve spans Maharashtra-Madhya Pradesh border with rich biodiversity.

name: Ramtek Temple
short_description: Ancient hilltop temple complex where Lord Ram is believed to have rested during his exile. Also associated with the poet Kalidasa.

name: Khandala
short_description: A scenic hill station adjacent to Lonavala, known for its stunning valley views, waterfalls during monsoon and lush greenery.

name: Karla Caves
short_description: Ancient rock-cut Buddhist shrine dating to 2nd century BCE, featuring India's largest Hinayana chaitya hall (prayer hall).

name: Nashik Kumbh Mela Site (Ramkund)
short_description: Sacred bathing ghat on the Godavari River, central to the Nashik Kumbh Mela held every 12 years. Lord Ram is believed to have bathed here during exile.

name: Chikhaldara Hill Station
short_description: The only coffee-growing hill station in Maharashtra at 1118m. The only place in Vidarbha where you can see tigers in the wild.

name: Akkalkot Swami Samarth Temple
short_description: Temple of Swami Samarth of Akkalkot, a revered saint who lived from approximately 1856 to 1878. Major spiritual destination in Solapur district.

name: Kanheri Caves
short_description: A group of 109 Buddhist rock-cut caves inside Sanjay Gandhi National Park, dating from 1st century BCE to 11th century CE.

name: Guhagar Beach
short_description: A pristine 6 km long beach on the Konkan coast with clean golden sand, relatively untouched by commercial tourism.

name: Venna Lake Mahabaleshwar
short_description: A beautiful artificial lake in Mahabaleshwar, popular for boating, horse rides and strawberry-picking nearby.

name: Kolad River Rafting
short_description: Maharashtra's most popular white-water river rafting destination on the Kundalika River, graded 3-4 rapids. Best during monsoon season.

name: Aurangabad Caves
short_description: 12 Buddhist rock-cut caves from 6th-11th century CE, featuring some of the finest examples of Tantric Buddhist art in India.

name: Bhaja Caves
short_description: 22 rock-cut Buddhist caves from 2nd century BCE featuring a large open-air chaitya hall and 14 stupas. Adjacent to the scenic Bhaja waterfall.

name: Wai (Mini Mahabaleshwar)
short_description: Known as Mini Mahabaleshwar. A historic town on the Krishna River with ancient ghats and temples, frequently used as Bollywood film location.

name: Amboli Hill Station
short_description: A biodiversity hotspot hill station in the Western Ghats receiving one of India's highest rainfalls. Home to rare endemic species of frogs and birds.

name: Nanded Gurudwara Hazur Sahib
short_description: One of the five Takhts (sacred seats of authority) in Sikhism. The final resting place of Guru Gobind Singh Ji. Major Sikh pilgrimage site.

name: Pawna Lake
short_description: A scenic reservoir surrounded by forts and hills, extremely popular for overnight camping, bonfires and sunrise views.

name: Harihareshwar
short_description: Known as the Devghar (home of Gods) of Konkan. Ancient Shiva temple on a cliff with beaches on three sides. Sacred to the Konkan people.

name: Diveagar Beach
short_description: An unspoiled Konkan beach famous for its clean white sand, turtle nesting sites and the rare Sonchafa flower found only here in Maharashtra.

name: Jejuri Khandoba Temple
short_description: Famous for the festival where devotees throw turmeric powder (bhandara) creating a golden spectacle. Important Khandoba (Shiva) temple of Maharashtra.

name: Bandra-Worli Sea Link
short_description: An 8-lane cable-stayed bridge spanning 4.7 km over the Arabian Sea connecting Bandra and Worli. An engineering marvel and iconic Mumbai landmark.

name: Saputara Hill Station
short_description: Maharashtra's only hill station in Gujarat border region on the Sahyadri range, known for tribal culture, Sarpagandha (snake plant) gardens and dense forests.

name: Kolhapur Palace Museum
short_description: Built in 1881 in Indo-Saracenic style, the New Palace now houses a museum with hunting trophies, royal armoury, photographs and memorabilia of the Kolhapur royal family.

name: Rankala Lake
short_description: A beautiful lake in the heart of Kolhapur city, popular for evening walks, boating and the scenic Temblai Temple on its banks.

name: Yawatmal Poacher's Lake
short_description: A serene lake near Yavatmal famous for migratory birds during winter. Part of the Vidarbha eco-tourism circuit.

name: Bhandardara
short_description: A scenic hill station around Wilson Dam on the Pravara River. Famous for fireflies in June, monsoon waterfalls and Ratangad fort trek.

name: Igatpuri
short_description: A scenic hill station on the Sahyadri range, home to the global headquarters of Vipassana meditation. Receives the highest rainfall in Maharashtra.

name: Solapur Siddheshwar Temple
short_description: 12th century Hemadpanthi-style temple built by the Yadava dynasty, dedicated to Lord Shiva. Set in a large garden complex with a sacred lake.

name: Mhaismal Hill Station
short_description: A small hill station on the Ajanta range at 1000m, offering panoramic views of the Deccan plateau. Known as the 'Mahabaleshwar of Marathwada'.

name: Chiplun
short_description: Scenic town on the Vashishti River estuary, known for the sacred Parshuram Temple, crocodile sanctuary and stunning river-meets-sea landscape.

name: Mahur Renukadevi Temple
short_description: One of the three-and-a-half Shaktipeethas of Maharashtra, dedicated to Goddess Renukadevi. Birthplace of the sage Parashurama.

name: Nagpur Futala Lake
short_description: A scenic lake in Nagpur city with a famous laser show, musical fountain and food stalls. Popular evening destination for city residents.

name: Jawhar Hill Station
short_description: Former princely state now a hill station known for Warli tribal art, Dabhosa waterfall (Maharashtra's highest) and panoramic Sahyadri views.

name: Ambazari Lake Nagpur
short_description: Nagpur's largest lake with beautifully maintained gardens, boating facilities and a children's park. Adjacent to the Ambazari Botanical Garden.

name: Dandeli Maharashtra Border
short_description: Adventure tourism destination near the Maharashtra-Karnataka-Goa tri-junction, offering river rafting, kayaking, jungle safaris and birdwatching.

name: Sevagraam Ashram
short_description: Mahatma Gandhi's headquarters from 1936-1948, from where he directed the Indian independence movement. Houses original huts and Gandhi's personal belongings.

name: Manmad Caves
short_description: Ancient rock-cut caves near Manmad railway junction with inscriptions and carvings, part of the Deccan rock-cut tradition.

name: Kamshet Paragliding
short_description: Maharashtra's premier paragliding destination at 625m altitude. Offers tandem flights and certified courses. India's largest paragliding school is located here.

name: Nagpur Maharajbag Zoo
short_description: One of the oldest zoos in India established in 1864, located in a heritage garden. Houses white tigers, leopards and over 100 species of animals and birds.
